data: Highest-cadence Falcon 9 pad on the planet — workhorse for ISS resupply + Starlink + national-security

Operational pad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. Originally Titan III / Titan IV (1965-2005); SpaceX leased and refit 2008; supports Falcon 9 commercial + national-security + Crew Dragon launches at the highest cadence of any orbital pad. AMOS-6 explosion 2016 forced a rebuild + capability upgrade. Coordinates from public FAA + USSF records.

Originally a Titan III / Titan IV pad from 1965 through 2005, refit by SpaceX in 2008 for Falcon 9. Today SLC-40 is the highest-cadence orbital pad ever operated, flying Starlink batches, commercial sats, ISS resupply via Cargo Dragon, and US national-security payloads. Rebuilt after the AMOS-6 explosion in September 2016 with an upgraded propellant system; the pad still does most of the SpaceX manifest the world sees.
Polar / sun-synchronous gateway — Falcon 9 to Starlink + national-security + earth-observation
